topic: Heitz-Neyret variance-preserving stochastic hex texture tiling vs linear barycentric contrast washout rig
topic_zh: Heitz-Neyret 保方差随机六边形纹理平铺对比朴素线性重心混合交界对比度洗白泥斑
scope: Deterministic Eric Heitz & Fabrice Neyret (2018) / Thomas Deliot & Eric Heitz (HPG 2019) variance-preserving barycentric stochastic texture tiling (C = mean + sum(w_k * (C_k - mean)) / sqrt(w1^2 + w2^2 + w3^2)) versus naive linear barycentric blending (sum(w_k * C_k)) and 64-node orthogonal harmonic spatial patch variance integration across 17 simplex transition stations (u in [0.00, 1.00]). No neural texture synthesis execution.

protocol.function: C_Heitz = c̄ + Σ w_k(C_k − c̄) / √(w₁² + w₂² + w₃²) → Triple-Junction σ(0.50) = 1.0000 (0.0000 Contrast Washout)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 simplex transition stations conserve full texture contrast variance without blurry ghost patches

good_fit: Aperiodic terrain, grass, gravel, concrete, and asphalt materials in UE5, Unity HDRP, Substance, and Three.js
Eliminating both periodic wallpaper grid repetition AND the −42.26% contrast washout blobs of linear hex/triangle blending
Normalizing mean-centered barycentric blends by √(w₁² + w₂² + w₃²) in 4 ALU instructions per pixel
Pairing with Geiss Triplanar Projection (Round 91) and Analytic Ray Footprints textureGrad (Round 61)
not_for: Regular man-made architectural tiles (chessboards, bathroom ceramic grids, brick walls) where strict periodic grid alignment is desired
Single-tap non-blended nearest-cell Voronoi lookup (which preserves variance but creates hard C⁻¹ seam cuts)
Neural diffusion texture generation or outpainting
